note: Default macro and behavioural assumptions for a Swiss resident. 'kind': 'observation' = the value is a published figure; 'assumption' = a modelling choice informed by the cited data. 'verified': true = the cited figures were checked against the source on 'retrieved'; false = rule of thumb or modelling choice with no checkable source (said explicitly in 'source').

assumptions.label: Average annual inflation (CPI)
assumptions.source: FSO CPI annual averages: +2.1% (2023), +1.1% (2024), +0.2% (2025) (https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/en/home/statistics/prices/consumer-price-index.html). SNB defines price stability as 0-2% and kept its policy rate at 0% on 24 Sep 2026 (https://www.snb.ch/en/publications/communication/press-releases-restricted/pre_20260924). 1% = mid-point of the SNB range, close to the 2023-2025 average (1.1%)

assumptions.label: Year-to-year volatility of inflation
assumptions.source: Modelling choice sized on the spread of recent FSO annual CPI changes (2.1%, 1.1%, 0.2% for 2023-2025; same FSO link as AS-inflation-mean)

assumptions.label: Real wage growth per year (on top of inflation)
assumptions.source: FSO Swiss Wage Index: real wages +1.6% in 2025 and +0.7% in 2024, after three years of decline (FSO release April 2026, https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/en/home/statistics/work-income/wages-income-employment-labour-costs/wage-index.html). 1% is a modelling choice: economy-wide averages are lower, young workers usually progress faster

assumptions.label: Assumed annual return of a balanced portfolio (nominal, after fees)
assumptions.source: Pictet 'Performance of Swiss shares and bonds 1926-2024': Swiss shares 7.7%/year, Swiss bonds 4.0%/year nominal; a 60/40 mix about 6% since 1900 (https://www.pictet.com/content/dam/www/documents/publications/shares-and-bonds-in-switzerland/2025/PWM_Performance-Swiss-shares-and-bonds-EN.pdf). We use a more prudent 4% for a 50/50 mix after ~0.5% fees, because CHF bond yields are now near zero; past returns do not guarantee future ones

assumptions.label: Annual volatility of the balanced portfolio
assumptions.source: Derived from Pictet 'Performance of Swiss shares and bonds 1926-2024' (2025 edition, Table 1): standard deviation of annual returns 19.9% (Swiss shares) and 3.9% (bonds), correlation 28%; a 50/50 mix gives about 10.7%/year (https://www.pictet.com/content/dam/www/documents/publications/shares-and-bonds-in-switzerland/2025/PWM_Performance-Swiss-shares-and-bonds-EN.pdf). Low end of the range: Pictet LPP/BVG-25 and -40 ESG-P fund factsheets show 4.5% and 5.5% volatility (31/10/2026). 10% kept as the rounded long-run value

assumptions.label: Interest on positive cash (savings account)
assumptions.source: Average Swiss savings account rate 0.11% (Jan 2026, 133 offers) and 0.12% (Feb 2026), Moneyland.ch (https://www.moneyland.ch/en/interest-rates-savings-analysis-january-2026); SNB policy rate 0% (https://www.snb.ch)

assumptions.label: Probability of losing the job in a given year
assumptions.source: SECO registered unemployment rate 2.9-3.0% in mid-2026, peak 3.2% in Feb 2026 (https://www.seco.admin.ch, https://www.amstat.ch). The engine uses it as the annual probability of losing the job. Cross-check with the inflow, which is the correct hazard: SECO 'Die Lage auf dem Arbeitsmarkt' December 2024, table 7, has 12,627 new registrations from employment in the month, about 152,000 a year or 3.5% of 4.35 million employed (one seasonally high month, so roughly 3-4%; https://www.newsd.admin.ch/newsd/message/attachments/91383.pdf). 3% sits inside that band; range 1-8% covers sectors and ages

assumptions.label: Average length of an unemployment spell
assumptions.source: SECO 'Die Lage auf dem Arbeitsmarkt', December 2024, table 5: average duration of registered unemployment 5.8 months (median 4.0); by age 3.2 (15-24), 5.4 (25-49), 7.5 (50-64) (https://www.newsd.admin.ch/newsd/message/attachments/91383.pdf). It is the elapsed duration of current spells, so completed spells are somewhat longer; unemployment insurance pays at most 520 daily allowances

assumptions.label: Share of income kept while unemployed (unemployment insurance)
assumptions.source: Swiss unemployment insurance pays 70% of the insured salary; 80% with dependent children under 25, an insured salary below CHF 3,797/month, or a disability of 40%+ (https://www.arbeit.swiss/secoalv/en/home/menue/stellensuchende/arbeitslos-was-tun-/finanzielles.html). Requires 12 months of contributions: students without them get 0

assumptions.label: Probability per year of an unexpected expense (health, repairs, family)
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, no official source: the FSO Household Budget Survey publishes no line for irregular one-off spending (checked 2026-11-21). Illustrates that budgets get surprises; range 0.1-0.8 per year is a judgement

assumptions.label: Average size of an unexpected expense
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, no official source: the FSO Household Budget Survey publishes no line for irregular one-off spending (checked 2026-11-21); about one month of a student's non-rent costs (EPFL budget: CHF 1,310/month without rent, https://www.epfl.ch/education/studies/finances-etudes/)

assumptions.label: Income tax level (1 = official ESTV 2026 tax at your residence)
assumptions.source: Tables: official ESTV tax calculator, tax year 2026, federal + cantonal + communal income tax with the standard deductions, no church tax, by city (12 cities of the UBS profiles) and household (single, married one earner, married with two children); core/data/tax_ch_2026.json, rebuilt by python -m core.bench.fetch_estv (https://swisstaxcalculator.estv.admin.ch). The value 1 = exactly those tables; the range 0.8-1.2 is a modelling choice for what the standard case leaves out (own deductions, pillar 3a, commune multipliers, church tax)

assumptions.label: Sell investments automatically when cash goes negative (1 = yes)
assumptions.source: Modelling rule (no external source): a shortfall is first covered by selling investments; any remaining negative cash is an unfunded financing need, not an assumed loan (UBS starter-kit convention)

assumptions.label: Emergency reserve considered healthy
assumptions.source: Value judgement, labelled: Swiss consumer advice recommends an emergency reserve of three months of expenses (six with irregular income), e.g. Beobachter 'So legen Sie Ihren Notgroschen richtig an' (https://www.beobachter.ch/geld/so-legen-sie-ihren-notgroschen-richtig-an-814025); no official federal or cantonal figure found (checked 2026-11-21)

assumptions.label: Debt payments above this share of income are considered stretched
assumptions.source: Value judgement inspired by the Swiss affordability practice: FINMA Supervisory Notice 02/2025 cites a 33% limit of sustainable GROSS income for mortgages, with an imputed 5% interest rate and 0.8% running costs (https://www.finma.ch/de/~/media/finma/dokumente/dokumentencenter/myfinma/4dokumentation/finma-aufsichtsmitteilungen/20250522-finma-aufsichtsmitteilung-02-2025.pdf). Ours is a simpler rule (actual debt payments vs net income) and is not a lending policy (checked 2026-11-21)

assumptions.label: Employee AHV/IV/EO contribution (share of gross salary)
assumptions.source: BSV synoptic table of contribution rates, state 1 Jan 2026: employee AHV 4.35% + IV 0.7% + EO 0.25% = 5.3% (same for the employer) (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/p1k1Z4DTI902/Entwicklung_Beitragss%C3%A4tze_2026.pdf); PwC Social security key figures 2026 (https://www.pwc.ch/en/publications/2026/Eckwerte%20Sozialversicherungen_EN_2026.pdf)

assumptions.label: Employee unemployment insurance (ALV) contribution
assumptions.source: 1.1% employee share on salary up to CHF 148,200/year, 2026 (BSV synoptic table https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/p1k1Z4DTI902/Entwicklung_Beitragss%C3%A4tze_2026.pdf; PwC 2026 https://www.pwc.ch/en/publications/2026/Eckwerte%20Sozialversicherungen_EN_2026.pdf)

assumptions.label: Insured-salary cap for ALV and accident insurance
assumptions.source: Maximum insured salary CHF 148,200/year, 2026 (BSV synoptic table https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/p1k1Z4DTI902/Entwicklung_Beitragss%C3%A4tze_2026.pdf; PwC 2026 https://www.pwc.ch/en/publications/2026/Eckwerte%20Sozialversicherungen_EN_2026.pdf)

assumptions.label: Employee non-occupational accident insurance (NBU)
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified: NBU (non-occupational accident) premiums are set by each insurer and risk class, deducted from the employee up to the insured-salary cap. No single official rate: Suva says its total premiums (occupational + non-occupational) fell to 1.9% of wages on average (https://www.suva.ch/de-ch/ueber-uns/magazin-und-medien/magazin/tiefe-preamien-2026); the ESTV calculator uses 0.4% by default. 1% kept inside 0.4-2% (checked 2026-11-21)

assumptions.label: BVG (pillar 2) entry threshold
assumptions.source: BSV key figures 2025/2026: entry threshold CHF 22,680, unchanged in 2026 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf)

assumptions.label: BVG coordination deduction
assumptions.source: BSV key figures 2025/2026: coordination deduction CHF 26,460 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf)

assumptions.label: BVG upper salary limit
assumptions.source: BSV key figures 2025/2026: upper limit of the insured salary CHF 90,720 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf)

assumptions.label: BVG minimum coordinated salary
assumptions.source: BSV key figures 2025/2026: minimum coordinated salary CHF 3,780 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf)

assumptions.label: BVG age credit, age 25-34 (share of coordinated salary)
assumptions.source: Art. 16 BVG age credits 7% / 10% / 15% / 18% for ages 25-34 / 35-44 / 45-54 / 55-65 (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1983/797_797_797/de#art_16); the BVG 21 reform that would have changed them was rejected

assumptions.label: BVG age credit, age 35-44
assumptions.source: Art. 16 BVG (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1983/797_797_797/de#art_16)

assumptions.label: BVG age credit, age 45-54
assumptions.source: Art. 16 BVG (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1983/797_797_797/de#art_16)

assumptions.label: BVG age credit, age 55-65
assumptions.source: Art. 16 BVG (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1983/797_797_797/de#art_16)

assumptions.label: Employee share of the BVG age credits
assumptions.source: Modelling choice (the legal bound is checked, the split of a given fund is not): the employer pays at least as much as all its employees together (Art. 66 BVG; BSV, https://www.bsv.admin.ch/de/finanzierung-der-beruflichen-vorsorge), so 0.5 is the employee maximum and the split of a minimum BVG plan, which is what the model computes (minimum age credits). Market average is lower: Swisscanto Pension Fund Study 2025 reports 36% employer vs 26% employee contributions in pension-fund inflows since 2008, an employee share of about 0.42 (https://www.zkb.ch/de/ueber-uns/medien/medienmitteilungen/2025/pensionskassenstudie-2025.html), but those plans also save more than the minimum; range 0.35-0.5 (checked 2026-11-21)

assumptions.label: BVG minimum interest on mandatory savings
assumptions.source: Federal Council kept the BVG minimum interest rate at 1.25% for 2026 (https://www.bsv.admin.ch/de/altersvorsorge-beruflichen-vorsorge)

assumptions.label: Effective income tax abroad (share of net salary)
assumptions.source: Modelling choice, not verified: one flat effective income-tax rate for a junior salary abroad, applied to the net salary after that country's social contributions. OECD Taxing Wages 2025 (2024 data), single worker at the average wage, income tax + employee contributions: Germany 37.4%, France 28.1%, Netherlands 27.2%, Portugal 25.0%, Spain 22.5% (country notes, e.g. https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2025/04/taxing-wages-2025-country-notes_16d47563/germany_59f2afde/510f880a-en.pdf); the income-tax-only rows at 67% of the average wage could not be read, so 15% (range 8-25%) stays a labelled assumption (checked 2026-11-21)

assumptions.label: Pillar 3a maximum per year, with a pension fund (BVG)
assumptions.source: Art. 7 para. 1 a BVV 3: 8% of the BVG upper limit (8% x CHF 90,720 = CHF 7,258), 2026, unchanged since 2025 (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1985/1778_1778_1778/de#art_7; BSV key figures 2025/2026 https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf). Not indexed in the model over the horizon

assumptions.label: Pillar 3a maximum per year, without a pension fund
assumptions.source: Art. 7 para. 1 b BVV 3: 20% of earned income, at most 40% of the BVG upper limit (CHF 36,288), 2026 (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1985/1778_1778_1778/de#art_7; https://www.bsv.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/GZplHByBJoFc/Internet_Masszahlenarticles_25_26_d.pdf)

assumptions.label: Pillar 3a maximum without a pension fund, share of earned income
assumptions.source: Art. 7 para. 1 b BVV 3 (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1985/1778_1778_1778/de#art_7). The model applies it to the gross salary when known, else to the net income (a slight underestimate)

assumptions.label: Return of the pillar 3a account per year
assumptions.source: Moneyland pillar 3a interest analysis 2026: unweighted average interest of pillar 3a savings accounts 0.21%/year in October 2026 across 93 providers, from 0% to about 1% (https://www.moneyland.ch/en/pillar-3a-analysis-interest-rates-2026). A 3a securities solution would earn about the investment return with its risk (range up to 4%). Deterministic, no volatility

assumptions.label: Exchange rate EURCHF (CHF per EUR)
assumptions.source: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rate, 20 Nov 2026: EUR 1 = CHF 0.9223 (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-daily.xml); October 2026 average 0.9282, last 90 days 0.914-0.948 (ECB 90-day history). Held constant over the horizon (no forecast); the weathers chf_strengthens / chf_weakens move it. The range is a modelling choice
